who: A. Bower (Adelbert Bower) Sageser, historian at Kansas State University; doctorate at Nebraska.

evidence.says: Identifies A. Bower Sageser as Adelbert Bower Sageser, author of The First Two Decades of the Pendleton Act (1935), and records the expanded name used on his thesis.
John D. Hicks identifies A. Bower Sageser of Kansas State University as a student who began doctoral work with him at Nebraska and completed it after Hicks left.
A September 1969 Journal of American History review names A. Bower Sageser and gives his affiliation as Kansas State University.

notes: Distinctive name, Nebraska doctoral history and Kansas State affiliation agree with the supervisor record.

who: Terry Lee Seip, historian at the University of Southern California, PhD Louisiana State University 1974.

evidence.says: Citations for The South Returns to Congress and We Shall Gladly Teach identify Terry L./Terry Lee Seip at the History Department, University of Southern California.
Lists Terry Lee Seip's Southern Representatives and Economic Measures During Reconstruction: A Quantitative and Analytical Study among LSU history dissertations from 1974.
USC lists Terry L. Seip as its 1990 recipient of the Associates Award for Excellence in Teaching.

notes: The LC record explicitly supplies the supervisor's university and expanded name; the doctoral record also agrees.

who: William H. Sewell Jr., historian of modern Europe at the University of Chicago, PhD Berkeley 1971.

evidence.says: Identifies William H. Sewell Jr. as Chicago's emeritus professor of political science and history, with a Berkeley PhD in 1971, and lists his books on French history and historical theory.
The candidate William H. Sewell is William Hamilton Sewell, a University of Wisconsin sociologist with a Minnesota PhD in sociology in 1939.
William H. (William Hawley) Sewell is the physician associated with Coronary Disease Management and a Yale medical degree.
Bill (William Shaw) Sewell is a historian at Saint Mary's University and author of Constructing Empire: The Japanese in Changchun, 1905-45.

notes: The listed authorities identify other people; none represents the Chicago historian William H. Sewell Jr. The superficially closest William H. Sewell authority is the Wisconsin sociologist.

who: Mark David Sheftall, historian of war and society at Auburn University, PhD history Duke 2002.

evidence.says: Auburn's 2009-2010 new-faculty brochure identifies Mark Sheftall as assistant professor of history specializing in war and society, with a history PhD from Duke.
Identifies Mark David Sheftall through The Glory and the Sadness (2002) and associates the record with Duke University.
Names Mark David Sheftall as author of Altered Memories of the Great War, a study of Britain and the Dominions' differing memories of World War I.

notes: Name, doctoral institution, period and war-history field agree. The matching candidate is Mark David Sheftall.

who: Caroline R. Sherman, early modern intellectual historian at Catholic University of America, PhD Princeton 2008.

evidence.says: The indexed university CV identifies Caroline R. Sherman as associate professor of history at Catholic University and gives her Princeton history PhD (2008), The Genealogy of Knowledge: The Godefroy Family, Erudition, and Legal-Historical Service to the State.
Identifies Caroline R. Sherman through The Genealogy of Knowledge (2008), with information supplied by Princeton University Archives.
Catholic University's 2016-2017 department highlights identify Caroline Sherman as associate professor of history and recipient of its 2017 teaching award.

notes: The exact dissertation title and Princeton year connect the LC candidate to the university historian. The CV text was available in the search index; its direct URL now returns 404.

who: James Henry Shideler, agricultural historian at UC Davis, PhD history Berkeley 1945.

evidence.says: Identifies James H. Shideler with UC Davis and cites the university memorial to James Henry Shideler, whose research concerned agrarian people and policies.
The university memorial states that James Henry Shideler completed his history PhD at Berkeley in 1945 and began teaching at Davis that year; it identifies Farm Crisis, 1919-1923 among his works.

notes: Name, field and exact doctoral institution/year identify the candidate. The supplied Wisconsin 1960 advising entry is not corroborated by these sources and remains an affiliation discrepancy.

who: Cristina Soriano, colonial Latin American and Caribbean historian at UT Austin, PhD history NYU 2011.

evidence.says: UT Austin's November 2024 event page identifies Cristina Soriano as associate professor of Latin American history in its History Department and author of Tides of Revolution (2018).
Lists Cristina Soriano, associate professor in the Department of History, with a New York University PhD from 2011.
Identifies the author of Tides of Revolution (2018) and coeditor of Cambridge Companion to Latin American Independence (2023); the latter citation explicitly names the University of Texas at Austin.
The other Cristina Soriano authority concerns a contributor to Trends in Cognitive Linguistics and researcher at the Swiss Center of Affective Sciences in Geneva.

notes: The UT affiliation, NYU doctorate and matching book identify n2018037086 as the historian.

who: Mack E. Thompson, historian and professor at UC Riverside, PhD Brown 1955.

evidence.says: Identifies Mack Thompson as a UC Riverside professor and dean, later AHA executive director, who earned his Brown PhD in 1955 with Moses Brown, a Man of Public Responsibility.
The exact-name candidate Mack Thompson is a bassist and guitarist credited on The Late Great Magic Sam; this is a musician's authority.
M. W. (Michael Welman) Thompson is identified through works including Novgorod the Great, The Medieval Hall and Medieval Bishops' Houses in England and Wales.

notes: None of the supplied authorities identifies the Riverside historian. The exact-name authority concerns a musician; the remaining candidates have different expanded names or works.
